key_insight: In surgically repaired congenital heart disease, true gaps in cardiology follow-up are common and are often linked to insurance instability and social vulnerability rather than medical need alone.
clinical_relevance: Missed follow-up can lead to silent disease progression and serious outcomes, including urgent intervention, stroke, infection, transplant referral, or death, even in patients with simple CHD.
method: Retrospective cohort of 1,746 patients with surgically repaired CHD at a tertiary center (2003–2020)
Combined electronic medical record data with structured manual chart review to distinguish true gaps in care from appropriate follow-up patterns
Defined gap in care as >3 years and 3 months between cardiology visits and beyond the recommended follow-up interval
evidence_signal: Large real-world dataset with adjudicated chart review: 52% screened as possible gaps, but only 15.7% were confirmed as true gaps in care.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective data may undercount social contributors and limit generalizability to other health systems, populations, and insurance environments.
paper_title: Gaps in Congenital Heart Disease Care: Social Drivers and Clinical Consequences
